messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: sustained increase in 429/503 rates on prod-inference-gateway · 5m window · 429_rate=4.8% · 5xx_rate=2.3% · p95 latency spiked to 1.9s. Dash: https://redwood.dash/g/inf/production?panel=429-503 (automated)
Maya: I'm oncall. I see the alert. Starting investigation — pulling up the live dashboard and request traces. Paging Jon as backup. @jon can you join? :phone:
pagerduty: Paging Jon (SRE) — triggered by escalation policy "prod-inference-oncall" for incident 2026-03-15T11:12Z
Jon: On it. Quick look: majority of 429s are coming from the inference gateway stage, large burst from a handful of tenants (tenant:acme-corp ~ 42% of 429s; tenant:bigticket ~ 18%). Also a cohort of long-lived streaming connections timing out and coming back with 503s.
Maya: Thanks. Initial hypothesis: a combination of aggressive client retries + a recent routing change that increased upstream load on the small-model pool. Can we triage by traffic-shaping and tenant caps? Need to limit blast radius.
Rachel: Suggest enabling tenant soft-caps for top offenders and globally throttle streaming connections. I can push quick rules to the gateway config if you want.
Jon: Yes please. Steps I'll take:
1) enable per-tenant rate-limit (soft) for top 10 tenants (reduce to 50% of current RPS)
2) apply streaming_conn_limit=200 on gateway (drop new streams)
3) divert non-critical inference traffic to fallback pool (lower-cost model) where feasible
Maya: Sounds good. Rachel, can you run the gateway rule change? I'll prepare the k8s patch for the ingress.
Rachel: Applying soft-limit for tenant:acme-corp now.
Rachel: ```
# gateway-cli apply-rate-limit --tenant acme-corp --rps 120 --soft
# gateway-cli apply-rate-limit --tenant bigticket --rps 80 --soft
``` 
Rachel: pushing streaming conn limit change to prod ingress (k8s annotation)
Rachel: ```
kubectl patch ingress prod-inference -n prod -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"gateway.streaming_conn_limit":"200"}}}'
``` 
Jon: I'm also firing an adaptive throttle in the routing plane for requests with seq_len>1024 to bias them to a fallthrough model variant.
Jon: ```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/routing/adjust -d '{"scope":"seq_long","action":"bias_variant","target":"small_mod_v2","weight":0.65}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Maya: Noted. Rolling these mitigations in now. I'll monitor 1,5,15 min windows. Can someone open a short incident doc? I'll capture timeline.
Ellie: I'll stub one in incidents/ with current hypothesis. Adding customer impact note — ACME support queue showing timeouts. Will inform CustomerSuccess.
Maya: Observability check: running live query for 429s by tenant and endpoint.
Maya: ```
SELECT tenant, count(*) as errors, sum(case when status=429 then 1 else 0 end) as r429
FROM prod.gateway.requests
WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY r429 desc
LIMIT 20;
```
Maya: ACME is top. Also seeing a spike in streaming session restarts from region us-west-2.
Jon: Mitigations deployed. Soft caps active, streaming conn limit set, routing bias applied. I'm watching envoy upstream_cx_overflow and 5xx counters.
Rachel: Confirming logs: gateway is returning fewer 429s to ACME since soft cap. 5m 429_rate dropped from 4.8% -> 2.1% in our staging window.
Maya: Good. Patch logs show some clients still aggressively retrying. Recommend we temporarily increase retry-backoff for internal LB and set Retry-After headers for 429 responses.
Jon: I'll push a header change to the gateway service to include Retry-After: 10 for 429s and 503s from inference upstreams.
Jon: ```
patch-service gateway --headers '{"Retry-After":"10"}' --status-codes '429,503'
``` 
Maya: Customer comms: Ellie, can you ask CS to surface ACME timeouts and hold off on any account changes until we confirm stability? Also request logs from ACME client to confirm retry behavior.
Ellie: on it. Pinged CS and included request for client logs. :white_check_mark:
Maya: Monitoring: p95 latency back to 1.1s, p50 stable, 5xx rate down to 0.9%, 429 rate 1.2% (10m avg). Dashboard: https://redwood.dash/g/inf/production?panel=429-503
Jon: Still seeing some error bursts correlated with a specific model shard (shard-17). I'm going to remove shard-17 from rotation for 10m to let it drain.
Jon: ```
admin-rotation remove --shard shard-17 --drain --duration 10m
```
Rachel: Removed shard-17. Health checks show node reclaiming and no increased errors elsewhere.
Maya: Good move. Observability: 429/503 trending down in us-west-2 and globally. Keep watching for client retries.
Maya: Next steps: (1) keep soft caps for 30m, (2) keep streaming_conn_limit until next update, (3) continue routing bias for seq_long for 20m, (4) have infra run a deeper health check on shard-17 and its kernel logs.
Jon: I'll run kernel and GPU health checks on shard-17 and open a ticket to infra if any signs of OOM or PCIe resets. Also will follow up on retry patterns with SDK team.
Maya: Handoff: my oncall ends in 25m. If still recovering at end of shift, I'll escalate to next oncall (Jon) for full incident lead.
pagerduty: Handoff reminder scheduled to Jon at 1779006000
Ellie: I've updated incident doc with mitigation steps and customer impact. CS is prepped to send a short notice to ACME once we stabilize (TBD).
Rachel: Monitoring for the next 10m: keep an eye on 429-rate by tenant and streaming_conn rejects. I'll alert if either goes above 2% or 50 rejections/min.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Quick check in 8 minutes.
Jon: 8 minute check: metrics still trending down. p95 0.95s, 429_rate 0.7%, 5xx 0.4%. I'm comfortable lowering routing bias from 0.65 to 0.55 to reduce impact on inference quality.
Jon: ```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/routing/adjust -d '{"scope":"seq_long","action":"bias_variant","target":"small_mod_v2","weight":0.55}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Maya: Agreed. Reduce pressure but keep caps.
Maya: Final check for now: 429s <1% and customer impact localized to ACME which CS is handling. I'll mark this thread as mitigation in progress. If we see regression, re-open paging.
sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied — rate limits, streaming_conn_limit, routing_bias, shard rotation. Current summary: 429_rate=0.8% · 5xx_rate=0.5% · p95=1.0s. Incident remains P2 (monitoring).
